clips.why: Arc of the video in one take: 'I fell for Opus 5... it felt more like a liability', Anthropic let the Opus line die, then shock that this is 5.5 not 5.1 and it's blowing him away -- cheaper, less bad at writing, better at code. Opening on 'Anthropic has released incredible stuff in the Fable line, but every other launch has been iffy' (32.2) also works; ending at 'blowing me away' (100.1) or 'Absolutely' (113.3) are both fine.

Fable has no zero-data-retention, so companies that need ZDR can't enable it; Opus can, so 'this model is almost immediately going to become the most popular for coding with AI by far, just from this one detail'.

Reads an Anthropic employee's tweet ('Opus 5.5 is way better than Opus 5. Sorry about that model') and argues it signals Anthropic loosening its leash on employees posting; lands on 'a very nice cultural change'.

'This model is cheaper, but not because it's more efficient': ~120k tokens per task vs 73k for Opus 5 and 27k for GPT-6 Astra; lands on 'doesn't matter if you're 2x faster if you need 4x more tokens'. Numbers are spoken, not just shown.

Disdain for max effort: it loops and burns tokens -- a max-effort thread ran 6.5 hours writing a markdown plan before he stopped it. Ending on 'apparently it only got halfway done' (1077.7) is also fine.

Evidence against max reasoning: on Skatebench going x-high to max took ~330 to ~5,000 tokens per question for a 1% score bump, 'a more than 10x increase in your costs for no good reason' -> 'don't use max on this model'.
Real work done in a day (visualizer, ports, finding a repo on his machine and merging a bug-fix PR end to end) cost 1% of his weekly limit -- 'They fixed the problem.'

His codebase-review bench showed Grok 4.7 punching above its weight; his theory is Cursor's Bugbot code-review data fine-tuned it. Self-contained hot take; 1330.4 adds 'Sol is good too, Opus and Fable less so'.
Gut-feel verdict: Opus 5.5 is the right default, Astra most thorough but spiky, but reach for Fable for front end -- marketing pages and design overhauls.

Quirk: paranoia about the context window, explained -- models trained before good compaction learned to fear the limit; OpenAI beat it out of theirs, 'Anthropic less so'. Starts on 'this model is not without its quirks' so the next line's 'ones' has its referent.

also_ok.why: Opus 5.5 moved the effort level out of the top of the system prompt, so changing reasoning level mid-session no longer busts the cache. Clean but ~18s.
Ex-Sora lead said you have to wait a week to see if a new Anthropic model is broken, then hours later: 'never mind, Opus 5.5 is crazy good'. Tidy anecdote, ~18s.
Longer version of one-percent-of-weekly that continues into 'I can't believe I'm saying this, but it's a way better value for your 200 bucks than a Codex sub'.

Good design instincts that don't show up in front end; Fable 5.1 had far better subtle taste; Opus demos are 'a little sloppy if I'm being real'. Opens on the 'Next, front end' run-up because it names the topic.
How much usage a $200 Claude sub now gets: 'running laps around our friends at OpenAI', though not on pure API prices.

negatives.why: WorkOS sponsor read (AuthMD, 'configuring Okta is hell').
Parallel sponsor read with a live speed race vs OpenAI search.
Opus 5 vs 5.5 example outputs read off the announcement ('that is absolute nonsense', 'three mdashes'); the point is the on-screen text.
Pareto frontier chart: 'Opus 5.5 has swept this line' -- a chart read aloud.
Fish-slop demo reaction ('look at the stingray... what the fuck') -- excitement about what's on screen.
Subscribe plea ('less than half of y'all are subbed').
